memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'From the fellowship offering you are to bring a food offering to the LORD: the internal organs and all the fat that is connected to them, both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which you will remove with the kidneys.'" - Lev 3:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The detail here can feel strange to modern readers, but the ancient worshipper understood it instantly. The fat was considered the richest, best part of the animal. The kidneys and the inner organs were, in Hebrew thought, the seat of the deepest emotions and hidden motives — the place we would today call the heart.

So what does God ask for from the celebration meal? The richest part, and the innermost part.

God is not content with the outer edges of our lives. He asks for what is most valuable and what is most hidden. Not the surface behaviour that everyone can see, but the interior places — the private thoughts, the buried motives, the things we would rather not examine.

David prayed, "Surely you desire truth in the inner parts" (Ps 51:6). Jesus told the Pharisees to first clean the inside of the cup and dish, and then the outside also will be clean (Mtt 23:26).

This is actually good news. God does not want a polished exterior from you. He wants the real interior — and He wants it not to shame you but because that is where genuine fellowship happens. Nobody has real friendship at arm's length.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What part of my inner life have I never honestly brought to God?
2. Am I offering God my best, or what is easiest to spare?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You ask for the innermost places, not just the presentable ones. I open them to You today, and I ask You to make them Yours. Amen.
